content:
I am trying to open the formalization of the existence of the complex structure on S^6 (https://github.com/plby/HopfProblem) locally. When compiling the original 250k lines file directly, it takes around 50GB of memory and crashes shortly afterwards. I tried asking an agent to split the project into multiple ~1000 line files, then open it locally. It has been compliing for multiple hours and doesn't seem to be close to reaching the end.
Are there any particular best practices to work with large Lean projects that would help me actually do it on an ordinary Mac Pro (Apple M3, 16GB RAM)?

You can try to splice it in small "chunks" to be compiled separately. But more often that not that is a flaw on the code or the proof, so you may as well ask the agent to audit the precise reason of the memory blowup. In my exeprience such high memory use rarely is required by the mathematics.

split the project into multiple ~1000 line files

So it's ~250 files each importing the previous one? If you run lake build <the_last_file> you should see some progress like [1/250] .... If memory blows up you can just kill lean and rerun and progress will not be lost, though it seems you're not reporting excessive memory use after splitting.
